Morphine is a naturally occurring opiate that exerts is main influence at the MOP receptor and results in analgesia as well as common side effects including sedation, respiratory depression, meiosis and constipation.

**Pain pathway and transmission:**

Afferent pain fibres (A Δ and C) carry stimuli from peripheral nociceptors to the dorsal grey horn of the spinal cord where they release Substance P which acts on NK1 receptors of second order neurones which carry impulses via the spinothalamic tract and spinoreticular tracts to the brain.

**Supra spinal MOP**

Descending inhibitory neurones /pathways arise from periaqueductal grey matter in the midbrain and rostral ventral medulla.

Descending neurones release Serotonin and Noradrenaline

→ inhibition of substance P realise

→ stimulates interneuron enkephalin release → Opioid receptors

Morphine → MOP agonism →   Inhibition of 'ON' Cell → ↑ 'OFF' cell impulses →  ↑ Descending pathway inhibition of pain transmission

**Spinal MOP**

Morphine act on Mu (MOP), Kappa (KOP) and Delta (DOP) G inhibitory protein coupled opioid receptors →↓cAMP → ↓pKa

→Presynaptically inhibits voltage gated Ca2+ channels →↓neurotransmitter release

→Postsynaptically→↑K+ efflux → hyperpolarisation → decreased neural transmission
